title: Adults with spontaneous aerobic Gram-negative bacillary meningitis admitted to the intensive care unit

claims.text: Escherichia coli was the most frequent pathogen in adult spontaneous aerobic Gram-negative bacillary meningitis, accounting for 57% of cases.
claims.byte_quote: Escherichia coli (57%) and Klebsiella pneumoniae (17%) were the most frequent pathogens.

claims.text: Klebsiella pneumoniae was the second most frequent pathogen, accounting for 17% of adult spontaneous aerobic Gram-negative bacillary meningitis cases.
claims.byte_quote: Escherichia coli (57%) and Klebsiella pneumoniae (17%) were the most frequent pathogens.

claims.text: The host population studied was adults admitted to the ICU with spontaneous aerobic Gram-negative bacillary meningitis (40 patients over 16 years across ten French hospitals).
claims.byte_quote: The study examined 40 adult ICU patients with spontaneous aerobic Gram-negative bacillary meningitis over 16 years across ten French hospitals.

claims.text: Most patients had predisposing risk factors, primarily chronic alcoholism and immunocompromised status; three immunosuppressed patients developed disseminated strongyloidiasis.
claims.byte_quote: Most patients had predisposing factors, primarily chronic alcoholism and immunocompromised status. Three immunosuppressed patients developed disseminated strongyloidiasis.

claims.text: CSF Gram's stain was positive in 85% of cases, CSF cultures positive in 98%, and blood cultures positive in 80%.
claims.byte_quote: Gram's stain, cerebrospinal fluid and blood cultures were positive for 85%, 98% and 80% of cases, respectively.

claims.text: Spontaneous aerobic Gram-negative bacillary meningitis is a rare complication of bacteraemia in adults.
claims.byte_quote: Spontaneous AGNBM is a rare complication of bacteraemia in adults.
